title_en: Intangible Cultural Heritage Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purpose of inheriting and carrying forward the fine traditional culture of the Chinese nation, promoting the construction of socialist spiritual civilization, and strengthening the protection and preservation of intangible cultural heritage.

Article 3 The State adopts measures such as identification, recording, and archiving to preserve intangible cultural heritage, and adopts measures such as inheritance and dissemination to protect intangible cultural heritage that reflects the fine traditional culture of the Chinese nation and has historical, literary, artistic, and scientific value.

Article 4 The protection of intangible cultural heritage shall focus on its authenticity, integrity, and inheritability, and shall be conducive to enhancing the cultural identity of the Chinese nation, safeguarding national unity and ethnic solidarity, and promoting social harmony and sustainable development.

Article 5 The use of intangible cultural heritage shall respect its form and content.
It is prohibited to use intangible cultural heritage by means of distortion, denigration, or the like.

Article 6 People's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate the protection and preservation of intangible cultural heritage into their plans for national economic and social development, and shall include the funds for such protection and preservation in their fiscal budgets.
The State supports the protection and preservation of intangible cultural heritage in ethnic minority areas, remote areas, and poverty-stricken areas.

Article 7 The competent department of culture under the State Council shall be responsible for the protection and preservation of intangible cultural heritage nationwide; the competent departments of culture under the local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the protection and preservation of intangible cultural heritage within their respective administrative regions.
Other relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, within the scope of their respective duties, be responsible for the protection and preservation of the related intangible cultural heritage.

Article 8 People's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the publicity of the protection of intangible cultural heritage, and raise the awareness of the whole society on the protection of intangible cultural heritage.
Article 9 The State encourages and supports citizens, legal persons, and other organizations to participate in the protection of intangible cultural heritage.

Article 10 Organizations and individuals that have made remarkable contributions in the protection of intangible cultural heritage shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 11 People's governments at or above the county level shall, as required by the work of protecting and preserving intangible cultural heritage, organize an investigation of intangible cultural heritage. The investigation of intangible cultural heritage shall be conducted by the competent department of culture.
Other relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level may investigate the intangible cultural heritage within their respective fields of work.

Article 12 When conducting an investigation of intangible cultural heritage, the competent department of culture and other relevant departments shall identify, record, and archive the intangible cultural heritage, and establish and improve a mechanism for sharing investigation information.
When conducting an investigation of intangible cultural heritage, the competent department of culture and other relevant departments shall collect representative physical objects that are part of the intangible cultural heritage, collate the materials obtained during the investigation, and properly keep them to prevent damage or loss. Photographs and duplicate copies of materials obtained by other relevant departments shall be submitted to the competent department of culture at the same level.

Article 13 The competent department of culture shall comprehensively understand the relevant information about intangible cultural heritage, and establish archives and related databases of intangible cultural heritage. Unless kept confidential according to law, the archives and related data information of intangible cultural heritage shall be made public to facilitate public access.
Article 14 Citizens, legal persons, and other organizations may conduct investigations of intangible cultural heritage according to law.

Article 15 Any overseas organization or individual conducting an investigation of intangible cultural heritage within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall report to and obtain the approval of the competent department of culture of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government; if the investigation is conducted in the administrative regions of two or more provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, the matter shall be reported to and approved by the competent department of culture under the State Council; after the conclusion of the investigation, a report on the investigation and photographs of physical objects and duplicate copies of materials obtained during the investigation shall be submitted to the competent department of culture that approved the investigation.
An overseas organization conducting an investigation of intangible cultural heritage within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall do so in cooperation with an academic research institution on intangible cultural heritage within the territory of China.

Article 16 When conducting an investigation of intangible cultural heritage, the consent of the subject of the investigation shall be obtained, its customs and habits shall be respected, and the lawful rights and interests thereof shall not be infringed upon.

Article 17 Where intangible cultural heritage items on the verge of extinction are discovered through investigation or other channels, the competent department of culture of the people's government at the county level shall immediately record them and collect relevant physical objects, or take other rescue preservation measures; for those that need to be inherited, effective measures shall be taken to support their inheritance.

Article 18 The State Council shall establish a national list of representative items of intangible cultural heritage, and shall include in the list for protection the intangible cultural heritage items that reflect the fine traditional culture of the Chinese nation and have significant historical, literary, artistic, and scientific value.
People's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall establish local lists of representative items of intangible cultural heritage, and shall include in the lists for protection the intangible cultural heritage items within their respective administrative regions that reflect the fine traditional culture of the Chinese nation and have historical, literary, artistic, and scientific value.

Article 20 Where citizens, legal persons, or other organizations consider that a certain item of intangible cultural heritage reflects the fine traditional culture of the Chinese nation and has significant historical, literary, artistic, and scientific value, they may propose to the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government or to the competent department of culture under the State Council that it be included in the national list of representative items of intangible cultural heritage.

Article 21 Where the same item of intangible cultural heritage maintains its complete form and content in two or more regions, it may be simultaneously included in the national list of representative items of intangible cultural heritage.

Article 22 The competent department of culture under the State Council shall organize expert evaluation panels and an expert evaluation committee to conduct preliminary evaluations and reviews of the intangible cultural heritage items recommended or proposed for inclusion in the national list of representative items of intangible cultural heritage.
The preliminary evaluation opinions shall be adopted by more than half of the members of the expert evaluation panel. The expert evaluation committee shall review the preliminary evaluation opinions and put forward review opinions.
The evaluation work shall follow the principles of openness, fairness, and impartiality.

Article 23 The competent department of culture under the State Council shall publicize the items to be included in the national list of representative items of intangible cultural heritage to solicit public opinions. The publicity period shall not be less than twenty days.

Article 24 The competent department of culture under the State Council shall, based on the review opinions of the expert evaluation committee and the results of public consultation, draw up the national list of representative items of intangible cultural heritage, and submit it to the State Council for approval and promulgation.

Article 25 The competent department of culture under the State Council shall organize the formulation of protection plans for the protection of the representative items of intangible cultural heritage at the national level.
The competent departments of culture under the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall organize the formulation of protection plans for the protection of the local representative items of intangible cultural heritage approved and promulgated by the people's governments at the corresponding level.
When formulating protection plans for representative items of intangible cultural heritage, priority protection shall be given to the representative items of intangible cultural heritage that are on the verge of extinction.

Article 26 For specific areas where representative items of intangible cultural heritage are concentrated, with distinctive characteristics and complete form and content, the local competent department of culture may formulate special protection plans, and implement regional overall protection upon approval by the people's government at the corresponding level. When deciding to implement regional overall protection of intangible cultural heritage, the will of the local residents shall be respected, and the physical objects and sites that are part of the intangible cultural heritage shall be protected to avoid damage.
Where the implementation of regional overall protection involves the spatial planning of villages, towns, or urban blocks where the intangible cultural heritage is concentrated, the local competent department of urban and rural planning shall formulate special protection plans in accordance with the relevant regulations.

Article 27 The competent department of culture under the State Council and the competent departments of culture under the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall supervise and inspect the implementation of the protection plans for representative items of intangible cultural heritage; if it is found that a protection plan has not been effectively implemented, they shall promptly correct and deal with the situation.
Article 28 The State encourages and supports the inheritance and dissemination of representative items of intangible cultural heritage.

Article 32 People's governments at or above the county level shall, in light of the actual circumstances, take effective measures, and organize the competent department of culture and other relevant departments to publicize and display representative items of intangible cultural heritage.

Article 33 The State encourages the conduct of scientific and technological research related to intangible cultural heritage and research on methods for the protection and preservation of intangible cultural heritage, and encourages activities such as the recording of intangible cultural heritage and the collation and publication of representative items of intangible cultural heritage.

Article 34 Schools shall, in accordance with the provisions of the competent department of education under the State Council, carry out relevant education on intangible cultural heritage.
News media shall carry out publicity of representative items of intangible cultural heritage and popularize knowledge about intangible cultural heritage.

Article 35 Public cultural institutions such as libraries, cultural centers, museums, and science and technology museums, as well as academic research institutions and protection institutions for intangible cultural heritage, and art performance troupes and performance venue operating units established with government funds, shall, within their respective scopes of business, carry out the collation, research, and academic exchange of intangible cultural heritage, and the publicity and display of representative items of intangible cultural heritage.

Article 36 The State encourages and supports citizens, legal persons, and other organizations in establishing, according to law, venues for displaying and inheriting intangible cultural heritage to display and inherit representative items of intangible cultural heritage.

Article 37 The State encourages and supports giving full play to the special advantages of intangible cultural heritage resources, and on the basis of effective protection, reasonably utilizing representative items of intangible cultural heritage to develop cultural products and cultural services with local or ethnic characteristics and market potential.
Where representative items of intangible cultural heritage are exploited and utilized, the representative bearers shall be supported in carrying out inheritance activities, and the physical objects and sites that are part of such items shall be protected.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall support entities that reasonably utilize representative items of intangible cultural heritage. Entities that reasonably utilize representative items of intangible cultural heritage shall enjoy the tax preferences prescribed by the State according to law.

Article 38 Where functionaries of the competent department of culture or other relevant departments neglect their duties, abuse their authority, or engage in malpractice for personal gain in the work of protecting and preserving intangible cultural heritage, they shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 39 Where functionaries of the competent department of culture or other relevant departments infringe upon the customs and habits of the subjects of investigation when conducting an investigation of intangible cultural heritage, causing serious consequences, they shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 40 Whoever, in violation of the provisions of this Law, damages physical objects or sites that are part of intangible cultural heritage, shall bear civil liability according to law; if the act constitutes a violation of public security administration, he or she shall be given a public security administration penalty according to law.

Article 41 Where an overseas organization violates the provisions of Article 15 of this Law, the competent department of culture shall order it to make corrections, give it a warning, confiscate its illegal gains and the physical objects and materials obtained during the investigation; if the circumstances are serious, it shall also impose a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan.
Where an overseas individual violates the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 15 of this Law, the competent department of culture shall order him or her to make corrections, give him or her a warning, confiscate his or her illegal gains and the physical objects and materials obtained during the investigation; if the circumstances are serious, it shall also impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan.
Article 42 Whoever violates the provisions of this Law and constitutes a crime shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.

Article 43 The measures for establishing local lists of representative items of intangible cultural heritage shall be formulated by the provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government by reference to the relevant provisions of this Law.

Article 44 Where the use of intangible cultural heritage involves intellectual property, the provisions of the relevant laws and administrative regulations shall apply.
Where other laws and administrative regulations have separate provisions on the protection of traditional medicine, traditional arts and crafts, etc., those provisions shall prevail.
Article 45 This Law shall come into force as of June 1, 2011.
